story_records.title: Cross-Discipline Technical War Room for NTP & Distribution UI Delivery
fields: NTP function testing was stalled, and Distribution UI delivery was at risk due to unresolved technical blockers and lack of alignment across disciplines.
Unblock testing and ensure 95%+ completion of Distribution UI delivery through rapid technical collaboration and escalation.

Convened a cross-discipline technical war room that produced a binding automation recommendation in under three hours; escalated to L2 environment owners and conducted targeted SME enablement sessions.
NTP testing unblocked and Distribution UI delivery achieved 95%+ completion.

story_records.title: Analytics Dashboard for Sprint Velocity & LLM-Retrospectives
fields: Delivery teams lacked visibility into sprint velocity trends and lacked structured input for retrospectives.
Architect and deliver a self-service analytics dashboard to surface performance metrics and automate retrospective insights.
Built a Next.js + Supabase application to expose sprint velocity KPIs and integrated LLM-powered insights for summarising historical team feedback and suggesting action items.
Improved delivery efficiency by 20% and operational clarity by 15% across core teams. Enabled data-driven sprint planning and retrospective cadence.

story_records.title: Cloud-Native Core Banking Transformation – 30% Faster Delivery
fields: ANZ’s core banking platforms were monolithic and delivered slowly; legacy architecture impeded agility and scalability.
Orchestrate end-to-end transformation of core banking platforms to cloud-native (.NET/Azure), while aligning to enterprise architecture and delivering measurable operational improvements.

Led program delivery for the transformation across 5+ cross-functional squads (up to 40 FTEs, including offshore teams), defining technical vision and backlog priorities to align with enterprise standards. Implemented CI/CD, DevOps, and MLOps patterns.
Cut end-to-end delivery time by >30% and infrastructure costs by >15%. Achieved 95% alignment with enterprise architecture standards and 100% compliance with risk models.

story_records.title: Executive Re-Baselining of Test Capacity for Payday Super
fields: The original Payday Super test capacity was fixed at 30 person-days, insufficient to cover required regression scope across 40+ scenarios and 11 data tables.
Produce a data-driven executive change request to re-baseline test capacity from 30 to up to 90 person-days, while ensuring auditability and risk governance.

Authored a comprehensive executive change request including options analysis, costed recommendation, and full Azure DevOps traceability across all scenarios and tables. Conducted risk assessment and quantitative sizing to justify expansion.
Change request approved and implemented, enabling adequate resource allocation to meet compliance and delivery commitments for STT regression scope.

story_records.title: Recovery of Infeasible SIT Window for Payday Super Reform
fields: The SIT (System Integration Testing) window for the Payday Super reform program was mathematically infeasible, requiring 75+ hours of manual evidence per team against only 64 available hours.
Re-engineer the testing execution plan to make the SIT window achievable within operational constraints while maintaining test coverage across 200+ SIT/E2E scenarios.

Architected and executed a six-day tiered test harness build with a formal go/no-go gate and a four-level contingency ladder. Collaborated cross-functionally in a technical war room convened under tight time pressure to produce a binding automation recommendation in under three hours.

Converted the infeasible plan into a deliverable one, enabling on-time SIT execution and program continuity. Unblocked stalled NTP function testing via L2 environment escalation and targeted SME enablement, and steered Distribution UI delivery to 95%+ completion.

story_records.title: Architecting COBOL/Mainframe Test Evidence Automation for 8 Squads
fields: The Payday Super reform program involved eight squads delivering integrated capabilities, but test evidence generation remained manual and time-intensive—averaging 3 hours per scenario—posing significant risk to compliance and delivery timelines.
Design and implement a zero-new-approvals test evidence automation strategy covering 200+ SIT/E2E scenarios across all squads, ensuring traceability and audit readiness.

Architected and deployed a toolchain using REXX, SMF, SDSF, PCOMM, PowerShell, and VBA to automate evidence capture from mainframe systems; integrated with Azure DevOps for full traceability across 40 scenarios and 11 data tables (AC6–AC19) with STT regression scope.

Reduced evidence effort from ~3 hours to ~15 minutes per scenario (≈92% reduction), enabled zero-new-approvals compliance, and supported executive re-baselining of test capacity from 30 to up to 90 person-days.

body.result: Cut end-to-end delivery time by >30% and infrastructure costs by >15%. Achieved 95% alignment with enterprise architecture standards and 100% compliance with risk models.

body.title: Executive Re-Baselining of Test Capacity for Payday Super
body.situation: The original Payday Super test capacity was fixed at 30 person-days, insufficient to cover required regression scope across 40+ scenarios and 11 data tables.
body.task: Produce a data-driven executive change request to re-baseline test capacity from 30 to up to 90 person-days, while ensuring auditability and risk governance.
body.action: Authored a comprehensive executive change request including options analysis, costed recommendation, and full Azure DevOps traceability across all scenarios and tables. Conducted risk assessment and quantitative sizing to justify expansion.
body.result: Change request approved and implemented, enabling adequate resource allocation to meet compliance and delivery commitments for STT regression scope.

body.title: Recovery of Infeasible SIT Window for Payday Super Reform
body.situation: The SIT (System Integration Testing) window for the Payday Super reform program was mathematically infeasible, requiring 75+ hours of manual evidence per team against only 64 available hours.
body.task: Re-engineer the testing execution plan to make the SIT window achievable within operational constraints while maintaining test coverage across 200+ SIT/E2E scenarios.
body.action: Architected and executed a six-day tiered test harness build with a formal go/no-go gate and a four-level contingency ladder. Collaborated cross-functionally in a technical war room convened under tight time pressure to produce a binding automation recommendation in under three hours.
body.result: Converted the infeasible plan into a deliverable one, enabling on-time SIT execution and program continuity. Unblocked stalled NTP function testing via L2 environment escalation and targeted SME enablement, and steered Distribution UI delivery to 95%+ completion.

body.title: Architecting COBOL/Mainframe Test Evidence Automation for 8 Squads
body.situation: The Payday Super reform program involved eight squads delivering integrated capabilities, but test evidence generation remained manual and time-intensive—averaging 3 hours per scenario—posing significant risk to compliance and delivery timelines.
body.task: Design and implement a zero-new-approvals test evidence automation strategy covering 200+ SIT/E2E scenarios across all squads, ensuring traceability and audit readiness.
body.action: Architected and deployed a toolchain using REXX, SMF, SDSF, PCOMM, PowerShell, and VBA to automate evidence capture from mainframe systems; integrated with Azure DevOps for full traceability across 40 scenarios and 11 data tables (AC6–AC19) with STT regression scope.
body.result: Reduced evidence effort from ~3 hours to ~15 minutes per scenario (≈92% reduction), enabled zero-new-approvals compliance, and supported executive re-baselining of test capacity from 30 to up to 90 person-days.
